scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in June/July to ~1180 in August and 1260 in September, roughly doubling, confirming the reported surge.

The observation shows that disputed bills are higher for actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating that the dispute surge is not solely driven by estimation errors; both read types contribute substantially.

The observation still shows that disputed bills are higher for actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240) (E-02). It no longer means that the higher actual-read count implies estimation errors due to missing reads are not a major driver; instead, estimated bill disputes are largely driven by AMI reads rejected for high consumption rather than missing reads (E-11).
The tariff change log shows no recorded tariff changes, indicating that tariff alterations are not a source of the recent billing discrepancies.
Field route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating missed or delayed manual meter reads that could contribute to estimation errors and billing disputes.

The observation still shows that field route completion for August‑September is 0.88 with 9,200 manual read accounts, below the 0.95 target (E-04). It no longer means that low completion directly leads to estimation errors causing disputed bills; the disputed estimated bills are primarily due to AMI reads rejected for high consumption, not missing reads from delayed manual reads (E-11).

The observation shows dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs SLA 3 days), indicating that the surge in disputes is not due to slow response; the issue likely lies elsewhere, such as bill correctness.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers, which can contribute to the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned, enabling retrieval of AMI read events; this does not directly address manual meter read errors or delays but removes a potential barrier to obtaining AMI data for billing.

The observation shows that a large subset of disputed estimated bills (1,184) had AMI reads recorded before the billing cutoff but were rejected due to high consumption, while a much smaller subset (56) lacked any AMI read. This indicates that many disputed bills stem from AMI reads being rejected (possibly due to validation rules) rather than missing reads.
